description: Chains, membership, the fork rule, cuts, content records and checkpoints end to end (sections 4.4, 5, 6, 9).

vectors.name: group/lifecycle-roles
vectors.description: Genesis, a writer, a reader. A reader's record and a stranger's are ignored. Carol's first record names a mhead from when she was a reader and stays ignored after she is promoted; her second, written after the promotion, is accepted.

vectors.name: group/remove-with-cut-unlisted-device
vectors.description: Bob writes twice on device b1 and once on device b2, then is removed (kind 5, which starts epoch 1 in the same record and is sealed under K_1) with a cut that lists only (b1, seq 1). His b1 seq 1 is accepted. His b1 seq 2 and 3 (beyond the cut) and every record on devices b2 and b3 (chains the cut does not list, including one from a device nobody had seen) are ignored when sealed in epoch 0. A record sealed in epoch 1 is ignored because he is not a writer as of its mhead.

vectors.name: group/removed-person-holds-only-the-old-key
vectors.description: The same records read by someone who holds only K_0 (the removed person): the removal, bob's record sealed with K_1 and alice's epoch-1 record are sealed under K_1 and wait for a key (no_key), so the chain stops at bob's addition and bob's records are judged as of it. There is no state of waiting for a new key for the group; this reader just cannot read on.

vectors.name: membership/remove-sealed-under-new-key-unreadable-with-old-key
vectors.description: The removal record opened with K_0 only: it is sealed under K_1, so it waits for a key (6.4: the removed person cannot read it).

vectors.name: membership/remove-opens-with-new-key
vectors.description: The same record opened with K_1.

vectors.name: group/lower-writer-then-raise-needs-new-epoch
vectors.description: A writer is lowered to reader with a cut, which needs no new epoch: a record beyond the cut (written with the old mhead) and one written as a reader are both ignored. Raising him again in the same epoch is invalid (6.2) and is ignored; after an epoch record the same raise is valid, and his record sealed in epoch 1 is accepted.

vectors.name: membership/kind-2-with-role-0-is-malformed
vectors.description: Kind 2 with role 0: removing a person is kind 5 (6.4), and role is 1, 2 or 3 (6.2). The payload does not have the shape the kind requires, so the record is discarded.

vectors.name: membership/kind-2-with-role-4-is-malformed
vectors.description: Kind 2 with role 4.

vectors.name: group/invalid-membership-records
vectors.description: Records that name the current head as mprev and are each invalid for a different reason (reasons in `ignored`); they are kept and ignored, and the one valid add continues the chain.

vectors.name: group/previous-key-mismatch-epoch
vectors.description: Two epoch (kind 3) records name the same mprev. One carries a key that does not match commit(0) as K_(e-1): it is ignored (previous_key_mismatch). The other carries K_0 and is valid.

vectors.name: group/previous-key-mismatch-remove
vectors.description: Two remove (kind 5) records name the same mprev. One carries a key that does not match commit(0) as K_(e-1): it is ignored (previous_key_mismatch). The other carries K_0 and is valid.

vectors.name: group/previous-key-mismatch-replace
vectors.description: Two replace (kind 4) records name the same mprev. One carries a key that does not match commit(0) as K_(e-1): it is ignored (previous_key_mismatch). The other carries K_0 and is valid.

vectors.name: group/fork-1-author-removed-by-another-candidate
vectors.description: carol adds erin; bob removes carol. carol has the smaller pid and would win step 2, but step 1 drops the candidate whose author is removed by another candidate, so the removal wins.

vectors.name: group/fork-1-author-lowered-by-another-candidate
vectors.description: carol adds erin; bob lowers carol to reader. Lowering counts like removal in step 1 (no epoch is needed for it).

vectors.name: group/fork-1-author-replaced-by-another-candidate
vectors.description: carol adds erin; bob replaces carol's secret. A replacement counts like a removal in step 1.

vectors.name: group/fork-1-mutual-removal-keeps-all
vectors.description: Each of carol and bob removes the other at the same mprev. Step 1 would drop both, so it keeps both and step 2 picks the smaller author: carol's removal of bob wins.

vectors.name: group/fork-2-least-author
vectors.description: carol and bob add different people at the same mprev; neither removes the other, so the smaller author (carol) wins. The loser and the record that follows it on its branch are ignored (lost_fork, off_chain).

vectors.name: group/fork-2-author-before-device
vectors.description: The candidate from the smaller author (carol) is on the greater device id; the other candidate (bob) is on the smaller one. The tuple is (author, device, seq, record_id) in that order, so the author decides: carol wins. An implementation that compares the device first picks the other.

vectors.name: group/fork-2-same-author-device-decides
vectors.description: One manager writes two different additions from two devices at the same mprev (two chains, so neither is a chain fork). The author is equal, so the smaller device id wins; the candidate from the greater device is listed first.

vectors.name: group/fork-2-same-author-and-device-seq-decides
vectors.description: One device writes two different additions that name the same mprev: seq 4 and then seq 5 on one chain (the second does not name the first; nothing forbids it). Author and device are equal, so the smaller seq wins; the later record is listed first.

vectors.name: group/fork-2-same-author-device-seq-is-a-chain-fork
vectors.description: Two additions with the same author, device and seq and the same mprev. Records that differ only in their record_id are a fork of the device chain (4.4): neither is accepted, so neither reaches the membership fork rule and the chain stays at carol's addition. The last comparison of 6.5 step 2 (record_id) therefore cannot decide anything in a full reader; the unit-level vectors group/resolve-record-id-* give it a job.

vectors.name: group/resolve-record-id-low-first
vectors.description: The 6.5 resolver given two candidates that differ only in record_id (listed with the smaller id first): the smaller record_id wins. This vector tests the resolver alone, because a full reader never reaches this case.

vectors.name: group/resolve-record-id-high-first
vectors.description: The 6.5 resolver given two candidates that differ only in record_id (listed with the greater id first): the smaller record_id wins. This vector tests the resolver alone, because a full reader never reaches this case.

vectors.name: group/fork-three-candidates
vectors.description: Three managers at the same mprev. bob removes carol; carol adds erin; alice adds frank. Step 1 drops carol's candidate (its author is removed by another), leaving bob's removal and alice's addition; step 2 picks the smaller author, alice.

vectors.name: group/fork-three-candidates-cycle
vectors.description: carol removes alice, alice removes bob, bob removes carol, all at the same mprev. Every candidate's author is removed by another, so step 1 drops them all and keeps them all; step 2 picks the smallest author, carol.

vectors.name: group/fork-remove-against-add-removal-wins
vectors.description: carol removes dave (kind 5, which starts epoch 1) while bob adds erin at the same mprev. Neither author is removed by the other, so the smaller author wins: the removal. Dave is out and epoch 1 is the epoch; a record naming the losing addition is ignored (its mhead is not on the chain).

vectors.name: group/fork-remove-against-add-addition-wins
vectors.description: bob removes dave (kind 5, which starts epoch 1) while carol adds erin at the same mprev. Neither author is removed by the other, so the smaller author wins: the addition. Dave stays a writer in epoch 0 and the epoch is 0; a record sealed under the losing removal's key K_1 is ignored because its epoch is not the epoch as of its mhead (6.5: only the key committed on the winning chain counts).

vectors.name: group/content-mhead-on-losing-branch
vectors.description: Two additions fork at one mprev; carol's wins. Erin's record names the winner as mhead: accepted. Records that name the losing addition as mhead are ignored, even from a manager (the author writes the change again). A record whose mhead nobody holds waits.

vectors.name: group/content-sealed-under-the-losing-key-of-one-epoch
vectors.description: Two epoch records (kind 3) for epoch 1 fork at one mprev and carry different keys; carol's wins. A content record sealed under the winning key is accepted; one sealed under the other key of epoch 1 names the winning epoch record as mhead but is ignored (wrong_epoch_key): only the key committed on the winning chain is that epoch's key.

vectors.name: group/genesis-duplicates-and-invalid
vectors.description: Two valid genesis records (same creator, nonce and K_0, different device and clock): the one with the smaller record_id is used and the other is ignored as a duplicate (6.1). Three invalid ones are ignored: a nonce that does not give the gid, a card that is not the creator's, a commitment that does not match K_0.

vectors.name: group/genesis-min-reader-2
vectors.description: Genesis names min_reader 2 and this implementation reads version 1: it MUST NOT read or write the group (6.1). It reports the group as unsupported and shows no state and no content.

vectors.name: group/genesis-min-reader-1
vectors.description: The same group with min_reader 1: read normally.

vectors.name: group/chain-fork
vectors.description: Bob's device b1 has two different records with seq 2. Neither is accepted, nothing later in the chain (seq 3) is accepted, seq 1 is; both are kept and the fork is shown. Alice's other chain is unaffected.

vectors.name: group/chain-duplicate-delivery
vectors.description: The same sealed record delivered twice (identical bytes) is one record.

vectors.name: group/chain-same-body-sealed-twice
vectors.description: A device seals the same body twice (same fields, same clock). Sealing is deterministic (4.1), so the two are the same bytes and the same record_id: one record, no fork (4.4).

vectors.name: group/chain-same-body-different-salt-is-rejected
vectors.description: The same fields sealed with a salt that is not the derived one (a device that draws a random salt): the reader recomputes the salt, finds a mismatch and discards the record (bad_salt). There is no second record at seq 2 and no fork.

vectors.name: group/chain-gap-and-prev-mismatch
vectors.description: Bob's b1 chain is missing seq 2 (seq 3 waits: gap). His b2 chain has a seq 2 whose prev is not the record the reader holds as seq 1 (waits: prev_mismatch). Both are "behind", never errors.

vectors.name: group/held-back-exactly-10-minutes
vectors.description: A record exactly 10 minutes ahead of the reader's time is accepted, and so is the one after it. The reader's time is BASE_MS + 5000.

vectors.name: group/held-back-one-ms-over
vectors.description: A record 10 minutes and 1 ms ahead is held back, and so is the next one (the same time); a record after those, with an ordinary time, waits behind them (gap): its chain has a hole until the reader's time catches up. The reader's time is BASE_MS + 5000.

vectors.name: group/held-back-membership-record
vectors.description: A membership record 10 minutes and 1 ms ahead is held back, so it is not on the chain; carol's record names it as mhead and waits (mhead_unknown), and bob's, which names the head before it, is accepted.

vectors.name: remember/same-state
vectors.description: A location offers exactly what the device accepted from it: nothing to report.

vectors.name: remember/offers-more
vectors.description: A location that offers more (a new record at seq 6) is not a rollback.

vectors.name: remember/offers-less
vectors.description: A location whose newest record of chain A is seq 4 while the device accepted seq 5 from it: rolled back, not treated as current.

vectors.name: remember/offers-nothing-of-a-chain
vectors.description: A location that no longer offers chain B at all.

vectors.name: remember/different-record-at-accepted-seq
vectors.description: A location offers a different record at seq 5 of chain A than the one the device accepted.

vectors.name: remember/different-and-same
vectors.description: A location that has both the accepted record and another at seq 5 is showing a fork, not a rollback.

vectors.name: remember/less-but-covered-by-a-checkpoint
vectors.description: A location dropped chain A's records up to seq 5, which a complete accepted checkpoint covers: not reported (the specification does not say; see findings).

vectors.name: remember/two-chains-one-rolled-back
vectors.description: One chain fine, the other behind: only the second is reported.

vectors.name: group/replace-secret-by-the-person-with-cut
vectors.description: Bob replaces his own secret (signed with the old key; kind 4 starts epoch 1 and is sealed under K_1) with a cut listing (b1, seq 1). The new pid takes bob's role. His b1 seq 1 is accepted, his b1 seq 2 and everything beyond the cut with the old key is ignored, and the new pid's record is accepted.

vectors.name: membership/replace-sealed-under-new-key-unreadable-with-old-key
vectors.description: The replace record opened with K_0 only: it is sealed under K_1, so it waits for a key.

vectors.name: group/replace-secret-rules
vectors.description: A replacement naming a pid that is already a member, one written by someone who is neither a manager nor the person, and one for a pid that is not a member are ignored; a manager's replacement is valid.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-full-history
vectors.description: Alice's items, a checkpoint by manager bob that restates the winning writes and covers alice's chain up to seq 5 and his own first record, then later records. All records present: covered content is folded as well, and the state is the one the records alone give.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-covered-records-deleted
vectors.description: The same group after the covered content records (alice seq 3 to 5) were deleted from storage. Alice's membership record at seq 6 is accepted only because the checkpoint covers the gap, and the state is the same.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-by-non-manager
vectors.description: A checkpoint written by a writer (not a manager) is ignored and covers nothing.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-history-records-present
vectors.description: Three passwords written in turn, then a checkpoint that carries the winner and one earlier write (history 1), then another record. With the records present the field's history is all earlier writes.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-history-survives-deletion-of-covered-records
vectors.description: The same group after the three covered records were deleted. The checkpoint carried the winning write and one earlier one, so Previous Passwords still holds "two"; the write it left out ("one") is forgotten.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-three-parts-order-1
vectors.description: One checkpoint in three records (parts 0, 1, 2 of one set), all present, records listed in another order each time. Alice's records at seq 3 to 6 (covered by part 0) were deleted from storage, so her seq 7 follows the covered range; `covered` and `purged` take effect because the set is complete: seq 7 is accepted and the first of bob's two writes of the secret is forgotten.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-three-parts-order-2
vectors.description: One checkpoint in three records (parts 0, 1, 2 of one set), all present, records listed in another order each time. Alice's records at seq 3 to 6 (covered by part 0) were deleted from storage, so her seq 7 follows the covered range; `covered` and `purged` take effect because the set is complete: seq 7 is accepted and the first of bob's two writes of the secret is forgotten.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-three-parts-order-3
vectors.description: One checkpoint in three records (parts 0, 1, 2 of one set), all present, records listed in another order each time. Alice's records at seq 3 to 6 (covered by part 0) were deleted from storage, so her seq 7 follows the covered range; `covered` and `purged` take effect because the set is complete: seq 7 is accepted and the first of bob's two writes of the secret is forgotten.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-three-parts-part-2-missing
vectors.description: The same records with part-2 of the set absent. The writes of the parts that are present fold at once; `covered` and `purged` take effect only when every part is accepted, so alice's seq 7 waits for the missing seq 3 to 6 and the first secret write is not forgotten.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-three-parts-part-1-missing
vectors.description: The same records with part-1 of the set absent. The writes of the parts that are present fold at once; `covered` and `purged` take effect only when every part is accepted, so alice's seq 7 waits for the missing seq 3 to 6 and the first secret write is not forgotten.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-three-parts-part-0-missing
vectors.description: The same records with part-0 of the set absent. The writes of the parts that are present fold at once; `covered` and `purged` take effect only when every part is accepted, so alice's seq 7 waits for the missing seq 3 to 6 and the first secret write is not forgotten.

vectors.name: group/purge-request-hides-at-once
vectors.description: Bob is a writer, not a manager. His purge request (kind 33) names the secret item: every reader hides it at once, though nothing has been removed yet. The other item is untouched.

vectors.name: group/purge-request-answered-by-a-managers-checkpoint
vectors.description: The manager's device answers with a checkpoint whose `purged` names the item up to its last write: the writes are forgotten and the request is answered, so nothing is hidden any more and the item is gone.

vectors.name: group/purge-request-by-a-reader-is-ignored
vectors.description: A purge request from a reader (not a writer) is ignored: nothing is hidden.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-purged
vectors.description: A manager's checkpoint names the item and the place of the second write in `purged`: the first two writes of its password are forgotten (no history), the third survives. A reader that still holds the records forgets them too.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-overlapping-order-1
vectors.description: Two checkpoints by two managers overlap: the first covers alice's chain up to q2, the second up to q3 (q2 is in both). Records listed with the first checkpoint first.

vectors.name: group/checkpoint-overlapping-order-2
vectors.description: The same records listed with the second checkpoint first (and in reverse): the same result.
